title: tradidi is general — the Supper is written; the rest is free order and decency
source_text: X. Sed, quod ad prius attinet, mirum est Bellarminum vim facere in voce tradidi, cum agnoscat ipse verbum tradendi generale esse, neque ad solam doctrinam non scriptam pertinere, sed ad doctrinam quoque scripto traditam. Et certe quae ibi tradit Paulus de institutione Coenae Dominicae, non tantum ab illo eo loci scripta sunt, sed a tribus etiam Evangelistis scripta reperiuntur, nempe, a Matthaeo, Marco, atque Luca. Cetera vero quae pollicetur Paulus se dispositurum quum venerit, merito nostri referunt, quicquid contra censeant Doctores Ecclesiae Romanae, ad ritus & ceremonias, & alia quae spectant decorum & ordinem, quaeque adeo sunt res per se liberae, & quae Ecclesiam ubique & semper non obstringunt, nec apud omnes eodem modo observantur. Et idcirco illa Pauli diatagmata sigillatim scribi necesse non fuit, cum in hoc negotio sufficiat regula Scripturae generalis, nempe, ut in Ecclesia omnia fiant ordine & decenter; particularis vero ordinis dispositio, & illius quod decorum spectat, Pastorum & Ecclesiarum ipsarum judicio & arbitrio relicta sit.
pass_a_gloss: But as for the former point, it is strange that Bellarmine presses force in the word I delivered, when he himself acknowledges that the verb to deliver is general, and does not pertain only to unwritten doctrine, but also to doctrine delivered in writing. And certainly what Paul there delivers concerning the institution of the Lord's Supper is not only written by him in that place, but is also found written by three Evangelists, namely Matthew, Mark, and Luke. But the rest which Paul promises he will arrange when he comes, our men rightly refer, whatever the Doctors of the Roman Church may think to the contrary, to rites and ceremonies, and other things which concern decorum and order, which are therefore things free in themselves, and which do not bind the Church everywhere and always, nor are observed among all in the same way. And therefore those arrangements of Paul did not need to be written one by one, since in this matter the general rule of Scripture suffices, namely, that in the Church all things be done in order and decently; but the particular disposition of order, and of what concerns decorum, is left to the judgment and choice of the Pastors and of the Churches themselves.
pass_b_english: Bellarmine already grants deliver is a general verb — written or unwritten.
The Supper institution Paul delivers is written in 1 Cor 11 and the Synoptics.
What he will arrange later is free order and decorum, not binding everywhere always.
1 Cor 14's general rule — all things decently and in order — is enough; particulars stay with pastors and churches.

lemmas.gloss: that the verb to deliver is general
let all things be done in order and decently

choices.term: neque ad solam doctrinam non scriptam pertinere
choices.english: does not pertain only to unwritten doctrine
choices.why: Cuts the specialty claim for oral tradition.
rejected: tradidi proves a second equal rule
